Holy cannoli. First of all, thank you all so so much. Things have been crazy here, thanks for all the thoughts and well-wishes. My grandmother died yesterday morning. She never woke up. By a lovely, I don't know, anti-coincidence, it happened sometime between 6:45, when I finally got some sleep, and 7:10, when I woke up.

One thing I didn't mention is that I wasn't alone through this. Her boyfriend was there. I couldn't be around him since we found out she didn't have long. He was a wreck. He was by her side constantly, but the few times he left her room, I found him staring outside and crying. I was almost more upset about him. He had gone through the same thing with his wife. Yesterday, he stayed with her until they collected her body. We had 6 people there, but not once did he join us. He left as soon as he could after that. My mother invited him for Christmas dinner, but he declined. He said he had to do some things at home.

The phone rang not two minutes after I got back. His daughter calling to say sorry for our loss, and to let us know that she wasn't alone. Her father had a heart attack this afternoon. I'm not exactly sure of the details, but his refusal of CPR was honored.

I've heard of people dying of a broken heart. Maybe, but I like to believe that even though they wouldn't be here, they could a least get each other one last gift. I'm not religious nor spiritual, at all, but I like to believe that somewhere they are together, forever
